Most modern medical ethics and legal frameworks do not support the idea that a hospital has a duty to provide substandard care to any patient, regardless of their age, disability, or other factors. In fact, the opposite is true: hospitals are legally and ethically obligated to provide care that meets the standard of care for all patients, without discrimination.

However, if you are looking for a legal argument that a hospital may not be held to the same standard of care for certain patients (e.g., due to resource limitations, end-of-life decisions, or other factors), that would be a different matter.
